problems.quote: Shaped grids are validated by vanilla's `ShapedRecipePattern`, so an oversized one is dropped with an error instead.
problems.issue: False. `ShapedRecipePattern.of(key, rows)` (build/neoForm/neoFormJoined1.21.1-20240808.144430/steps/unzipSources/unpacked/net/minecraft/world/item/crafting/ShapedRecipePattern.java:83-86) goes straight to `unpack()`, and `unpack()` (lines 88-113) checks only for an undefined symbol and for key symbols unused by the pattern. The size limits ('too many rows', 'too many columns', 'each row must be the same width') live exclusively in `Data.PATTERN_CODEC` (lines 239-259), which is only used when decoding a recipe from JSON — `of()` never touches it. `ShapedRecipe`'s constructor (ShapedRecipe.java:21-30) validates nothing either. A pattern like `AAAA|AAAA|AAAA|AAAA` therefore builds a 4x4 ShapedRecipePattern without any error, is registered, and is exactly as silently unmatchable as the oversized shapeless recipe the row is contrasting it with. (Ragged rows are a different case: they die in `shrink()`'s `substring` with a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, not in a size check.)
problems.correction: The shaped side is no better off: nothing checks the grid size either. A pattern wider or taller than 3 is built and registered without a word and simply never matches a crafting table. Only ragged rows and undefined symbols are caught.

problems.quote: | Grid malformed — ragged rows, more than 3×3, a symbol used but not defined |
problems.issue: The 'more than 3×3' item does not belong in the dropped-entry table — see above, `ShapedRecipePattern.of` applies no size limit, so an oversized grid is never dropped and never logs anything. The other two items in the cell (ragged rows, undefined symbol) are correct.
problems.correction: Drop 'more than 3×3' from the cell, leaving 'ragged rows, a symbol used but not defined' (and optionally 'a key symbol the pattern never uses', which vanilla also rejects).
